panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: This panel is a radiograph illustrating C&O Type I, which involves fibrous ankylosis. This is a direct presentation of the target disease. [raw subtype: C&O Type I; CMPOS Type I] B: The panel shows osseous synostosis between the proximal radius and ulna, which is characteristic of C&O Type II. [raw subtype: C&O Type II; CMPOS Type II] C: The panel shows fusion combined with radiographic signs of a hypoplastic and dislocated radial head, fitting C&O Type III. [raw subtype: C&O Type III; CMPOS Type III] D: This panel illustrates C&O Type IV, which involves pseudo-synostosis and specific radial head deformation/dislocation, fitting the disease profile. [raw subtype: C&O Type IV; CMPOS Type II]

in_text_mentions: C&O classification consists of four types: (I) fibrous ankylosis with normal radial head; (II) osseous synostosis with normal radial head; (III) osseous synostosis with posteriorly dislocated and hypoplastic radial head; (IV) pseudo-synostosis and anteriorly dislocated, mushroom-shaped radial head (11). CMPOS classification consists of three type: (I) fibrous pseudo-synostosis with any shape of the radial head; (II) osseous synostosis with or without dislocated radial head; (III) radiographic radial head unobservable and osseous synostosis with the ulna (12) (see Figure 1).
